title: Public art funding and a possible regional arts council
subtitle: Also: write-off of uncollectible accounts, closed session on water capacity litigation and police board budget
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended up to $600,000 from the Public Art Reserve for a permanent artwork at the Kitchener Central Transit Hub {{vote:m3}}. It also recommended changing the source of $300,000 already earmarked for the artwork from the 2026 Transit capital budget to the general tax supported capital reserve. Staff plan a national call for artists in the first quarter of 2026.

The committee also recommended that staff consult the arts community and the public on creating a Waterloo Region Arts Council and report back by August 2026 {{vote:m4}}. This follows a review of how arts funding is delivered. Staff reported no clear consensus among area municipalities on an arts council.

On the consent agenda, the committee recommended writing off $113,335.76 in uncollectible accounts for 2025 {{vote:m1}}. A motion on Budget 2027 from a councillor was withdrawn. The committee then moved into closed session on legal advice about potential litigation over water capacity and the Waterloo Police Services Board budget approval. The minutes report no outcomes from that session.

decisions.item: Public art for Kitchener Central Transit Hub
decisions.detail: The committee recommended spending up to $600,000 from the Public Art Reserve on permanent public art and moving $300,000 of earmarked funding from the 2026 Transit capital budget to the general tax supported capital reserve.
The committee recommended directing staff to consult the arts community and the public on creating a Waterloo Region Arts Council and to report back by August 2026.
As part of the consent agenda, the committee recommended writing off $113,335.76 in accounts receivable for the year ended December 31, 2025.

debate: On the transit hub art, one councillor asked how the money was accounted for. Staff explained that $300,000 had accumulated in the Public Art Reserve and that the project budget had also carried $300,000. Staff said $600,000 is what is needed for an appropriate piece.

A member of the Public Art Advisory Committee supported the recommendation. The member said the committee was already refining the call for artists, which staff said would be national because the project is high profile.

On the arts council, the sponsoring councillor said arts groups had asked for a more coordinated way to speak with one voice and to have clearer funding opportunities. The sponsor said the consultation fits the Region's practice of engaging the community before making decisions.

One councillor supported the motion but flagged concern about scope creep, since arts and culture are mainly an area municipal responsibility and the public wants less duplication. Another supporter pointed to the former arts council's record of funding many projects over the years.
A councillor asked whether film development could fall under the arts work. Staff said lens-based art overlaps with film but commercial film development, such as a film office, is a separate matter.
